newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner's Time new media head to resign.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner's Time new media head to resign.

text.p: Time Warner Inc's Time Inc said on Friday Paul Sagan, president and editor of its new media division which oversees Time's on-line and Internet businesses, planned to resign from the company at the end of the year.
Sagan said it was a personal decision, made so that he could spend more time with his children.
"This decision does not in any way reflect unhappiness with my assignment," said Sagan, who became president and editor of new media in January 1996.
"Rather, this is a personal decision to allow my wife and me to spend more time with our children, to travel with them, and to educate them in different parts of the world," he said.
Time said a successor would be named to replace Sagan by the end of the year.
The company also said it remained committed to new media and confident in its strategy to move the business forward.
Time Warner recruited Sagan in 1991 to design and launch its cable news channel, New York 1 News. Sagan began working at Time Inc in 1993 when he was named managing editor of its News on Demand.
